title: Veteran Bradley Beal returning to Clippers on 2-year deal: Agent
content:
The LA Clippers and shooting guard Bradley Beal have agreed to a two-year deal worth $13.2 million, his agent Mark Bartelstein confirmed to The Athletic on Thursday.

The second year of the deal is a player option partially guaranteed for $3 million, according to league sources speaking on the condition of anonymity because the deal is not yet finalized.

NBA reporter Chris Haynes first reported Beal’s agreement.

The Clippers originally agreed to a two-year contract with Beal last offseason, which included a player option, following a buyout agreement that Beal reached with the Phoenix Suns. But Beal’s 2025-26 season never got off the ground, as he was limited in the preseason due to left knee inflammation.

Despite being on a strict minutes restriction, the Clippers started Beal at shooting guard. He also missed time due to a back injury suffered when he drew a charge against the Suns in the season’s opening week, costing him two games. Beal’s season came to an end after he suffered a left hip fracture against the Suns in November, appearing in only six games and zero fourth quarters. In those six games, the three-time All-Star averaged 8.2 points and shot 36.8 percent from 3.

This story will be updated.
